name: Nematodes: Ascaris, Hookworm, Strongyloides, Enterobius and Filariae
aliases: Filariae: Wuchereria, Loa, Onchocerca and Dracunculus

reference.source: Paniker's Textbook of Medical Parasitology 8th Ed + Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology (topic maps; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Night itch: NIH swab, family treats
reference.pathophysiology: Larval lung passage sensitises eosinophils into Loeffler showers while adult boluses plug ileum; Wolbachia drives filarial lymphangitis until doxycycline sterilises, and Strongyloides rhabditiform larvae recycle internally for decades.
additionalDifferentials: Ascaris versus hookworm by eggs and anaemia
Strongyloides versus hookworm by autoinfection and steroids risk
Loa versus Wuchereria by eye worm and periodicity
additionalInvestigations: Stool concentration with NIH swab in nocturnal itch
Night blood smears with DEC provocation in filarial swelling
Muscle biopsy with eosinophils in pork myalgia
